newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 4.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 4.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Tuesday:
* On Monday, the Dow Jones dropped 6.93 points to 6,806.16. PLDT's ADR shed $0 3/8 to $59.
* The peso closed at 26.335 to a U.S. dollar from 26.349.
* The Philippine Stock Exchange composite index ended at an all time high of 3,447.60 points, up 25.69.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was steady at 10.53125 percent.

*Filinvest Land Inc (FLI), a unit of Filinvest Development Corp, said on Monday it logged a 102 percent jump in 1996 net income to 2.04 billion pesos from 1.01 billion pesos in 1995 on account of robust sales from its housing projects.
*Fil-Estate Land Inc said on Monday it made a group net income of 455.02 million pesos in the first three months ended December 31, 1996 compared with 312.63 million pesos in the year-ago quarter.
*The Philippine Supreme Court on Monday awarded the sale of the historic Manila Hotel to a Filipino company, throwing out the winning bid of Malaysian infrastructure development firm Renong Berhad.
*Alaska Milk Corp said its net income in 1996 dropped to 116 million pesos from the year-ago 212 million.
*SolidBank said its 1996 net increased to 623 million pesos from the previous 550 million.
*First Philippine Holdings Corp posted a net income of 970.643 million pesos in the first six months ended December 31, documents submitted to the Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday showed.
*Union Bank of the Philippines said on Monday its unaudited net income in 1996 reached 961.8 million pesos, 32 percent higher than 729 million pesos in 1995.
*Far East Bank and Trust Co, one of the largest banks in the country, said on Monday unaudited net income rose by about 28 percent to 2.26 billion pesos in 1996 from 1.76 billion pesos in 1995.
*The Philippines' 91-day Treasury bill rate was marginally higher at 10.693 percent at the weekly auction on Monday, against 10.673 percent registered last week, the Bureau of Treasury said.

*Retailer Uniwide Holdings Inc's 1996 net profits may likely hit 760 million pesos against an earlier forecast of 731 million pesos, the firm's chief financial officer Jaime Cabangis told Reuters on Monday.
Cabangis said the firm expects its bottom line earnings in 1997 to grow by 25 to 30 percent from the 1996 level.
The firm posted a net income of 111.6 million pesos in 1995.
*Easycall said on Monday its net income from July to December 1996, or the first six months of its current fiscal year, reached 30.986 million pesos.
*Cellular firm and paging operator Pilipino Telephone Corp (Piletel) said on Monday it sees its net income for 1996 "in the vicinity" of 700 million pesos.
